transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. Could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Nice to meet you too, Dr. Smith. Well... I guess what finally scared me into actually making this appointment is that I’ve been having these thoughts lately. 

I don't want to hurt myself—I want to be clear about that—but I keep catching myself thinking things like, well, if I just didn’t wake up tomorrow, that might be easier. It just really unsettled me to realize I was thinking that way, so I figured it was time to come in and talk to someone.
How long have you been feeling this way?

It's been about six months now. Just this... low, flat feeling that won't seem to lift. It's been going on long enough that my usual routines just don't help anymore. Like, I usually take morning walks or go to my art classes, but they've completely stopped feeling restorative to me.
Have you ever experienced a period like this before in your life, where you felt this low and flat for several months at a time?
No, not really. I mean, everyone has bad days or tough weeks, but nothing like this. I've never had this kind of heavy, flat feeling stretch on for months. This is definitely a first for me.
Are you currently able to continue going to work or managing your basic household responsibilities, or have you had to stop doing those things entirely?

I haven't had to stop entirely. I'm still getting to work, and I'm taking care of myself at home. But... things are definitely slipping a bit. 

At the store—I supervise retail staff—I've started avoiding any extra conversations with my team. I just kind of keep to myself and only talk when I absolutely have to. And I'm finding myself putting off really simple store decisions, mostly because I just don't trust my own judgment right now. So I am managing the basics, but I'm definitely not operating the way I normally would.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your sleep patterns since you started feeling this way six months ago?
Not really, no. My sleep has been... pretty much the same as always. I still go to bed around my usual time and wake up for work like normal. I haven't noticed any big changes there, honestly.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your appetite or the way you've been eating over these past six months?

No, I haven't really noticed any changes there. I mean, my appetite is pretty much the same as it's always been. I'm still eating my regular meals, and I haven't noticed my clothes fitting any differently or anything like that. So... no, my eating habits haven't really changed.
How would you describe your overall sense of self-worth or confidence in yourself during these past six months?

Well, my confidence has definitely taken a hit. I just... I feel really down on myself lately. I keep replaying these little mistakes at work in my head. Like, if a display sign is crooked or if one of the new trainees looks confused, I just fixate on it. I start telling myself that I'm a useless supervisor and that I'm not doing a good job anymore. It's just this constant feeling that I'm not good enough.
During these past six months, have you had any stretches of a few weeks or more where you felt like your old self again, or has this low, flat feeling been present almost every single day?

No, I haven't really had any stretches like that where I felt like my old self. It's been almost every single day. This low, flat feeling has just... it's been present for about six months now without a break. It's been going on long enough that my usual routines, like going to my art classes or taking my morning walks, they just stopped feeling restorative. I still try to do them, but they don't really do anything to lift that flat feeling anymore.
Have you noticed that your movements or the speed at which you speak have become noticeably slower or more agitated since this started?

Well, yes, I suppose I have. It kind of goes both ways, depending on the day. Some days I'll catch myself just pacing around the living room and picking at my cuticles, feeling a bit restless. But then other days... it's the exact opposite. Even just walking from the break room out to the sales floor feels strangely slow, like it takes more effort to just move normally.
Have you noticed any difficulty concentrating on tasks or making decisions beyond the ones you mentioned at work?

Yes, I definitely have. It's... well, decisions that used to be completely automatic just aren't right now. Like at work, trying to choose which endcap to reset first, or even just at home figuring out what blouse to wear for the day. I'll just find myself standing there, feeling really foggy, and second-guessing myself over the smallest things. It's just hard to think clearly lately.
